reviews.title: Fly.
reviews.text:
The Flying Gorilla

My life had been going downhill for a long time.

It felt like every day was the same.

I would wake up, stare at the ceiling for a few minutes, and wonder why I even bothered getting out of bed. School wasn’t going well. My grades were terrible. I was constantly tired. My friends were slowly drifting away, and even when I tried talking to people, I somehow managed to make everything awkward.

Nothing was working.

I tried sports.

I tried gaming.

I tried watching shows.

I even tried going outside more.

Nothing changed.

One night, after an especially terrible day, I came home, threw my backpack on the floor, and sat on my bed.

I picked up my phone.

I scrolled through TikTok.

Nothing.

Instagram.

Nothing.

YouTube.

Nothing.

Then I saw it.

A video of a gorilla.

Flying.

Not metaphorically.

Not with wings.

Just a massive gorilla flying through the sky like it had somewhere extremely important to be.

The caption said:

“Flying Gorilla.”

I stared at the screen.

“What is this?”

I clicked on the game.

The screenshots looked ridiculous.

The gorilla had absolutely no business being in the sky.

I downloaded it.

The game opened.

There it was.

A gorilla.

Flying.

I started laughing.

For the first time in weeks, I actually laughed.

I played one round.

Then another.

Then another.

The game was unbelievably stupid.

And somehow, it was incredible.

I didn’t care about my problems for those few minutes.

I was just focused on making a gorilla fly.

That night, I went to sleep happier than I had in a long time.

The next morning, something was different.

I woke up and immediately thought about Flying Gorilla.

I played a few rounds before school.

I started getting better.

I learned how to control the gorilla.

I learned the maps.

I learned the best routes.

I started setting personal records.

Then something strange happened.

I started applying the same mindset to everything else.

I realized I had been giving up way too easily.

If I could spend hours trying to improve at controlling a flying gorilla, why couldn’t I improve at everything else?

So I started with school.

My grades were awful.

But instead of saying, “I’m just bad at this,” I started thinking:

“Not yet.”

I studied.

I asked questions.

I did my homework.

At first, nothing changed.

Then I got my first good grade.

It wasn’t an A.

It wasn’t even close.

But it was better.

I smiled.

I realized something.

Progress was progress.

The same thing happened with baseball.

I had been frustrated because I wasn’t as good as I wanted to be.

My throws weren’t perfect.

My swing wasn’t perfect.

I made mistakes.

But instead of getting angry every time I messed up, I started practicing.

Every throw was another attempt.

Every swing was another attempt.

Every mistake was another chance to improve.

Slowly, I got better.

My friends started noticing.

“Bro, what happened to you?”

I just smiled.

“Flying Gorilla.”

They thought I was joking.

I wasn’t.

Eventually, I started talking to people again.

I apologized to people I had treated badly.

I started helping people instead of making fun of them.

I became more patient.

I became more confident.

I stopped blaming everyone else for my problems.

I realized that I had made plenty of mistakes.

I couldn’t change what I had done.

But I could change what I did next.

Months passed.

My grades improved.

My baseball improved.

My relationships improved.

Even my family noticed.

One night, my dad looked at me and said:

“You seem different.”

I thought about it.

“I am.”

“What happened?”

I looked down at my phone.

The Flying Gorilla icon was sitting on my home screen.

I laughed.

“You wouldn’t believe me.”

Eventually, I became known as the Flying Gorilla guy.

Not because I talked about it constantly.

But because whenever something went wrong, I would say:

“Keep flying.”

People started laughing at first.

Then they started saying it too.

Someone failed a test.

“Keep flying.”

Someone struck out.

“Keep flying.”

Someone got rejected.

“Keep flying.”

It became our thing.

Years later, I looked back at the person I used to be.

I barely recognized him.

He had been angry.

Lost.

Unmotivated.

He thought his life was already decided.

But he had been wrong.

His life wasn’t over.

He just needed something stupid enough to make him laugh again.

And somehow, that something was a flying gorilla.

I never became perfect.

I still had bad days.

I still made mistakes.

I still failed sometimes.

But I wasn’t the same person anymore.

I had learned that redemption doesn’t happen all at once.

You don’t wake up one morning and suddenly become a completely different person.

It happens through tiny choices.

One good decision.

Then another.

Then another.

Until one day you look back and realize how far you’ve come.

And whenever life got difficult, I remembered the most important lesson I had ever learned:

Even when everything feels impossible…

You can still fly.

I opened Flying Gorilla one last time.

The gorilla launched into the sky.

I watched it soar across the screen.

I smiled.

“Thanks, buddy.”

Then I closed the app.

Because I didn’t need it anymore.

The gorilla had done its job.

It had saved me.

Not because it was magical.

Not because it gave me superpowers.

But because it reminded me that sometimes life doesn’t need a perfect solution.

Sometimes you just need one stupid little reason to keep going.

And for me…

That reason was a flying gorilla.
